# Perform Cook-Weisberg test for heteroscedasticity

<small>Source: [`man/performCookWeisbergTest.Rd`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/heteroTests/blob/main/man/performCookWeisbergTest.Rd) · Help: `?performCookWeisbergTest`</small>

The Cook-Weisberg (1983) score test, with the fitted values as the sole variance regressor by default, or against a variance model given by `var_formula`. Since 0.14.0 it is the one entry point for the test; [`performNCVTest`](performNCVTest.md) is deprecated.

## Usage

```r
performCookWeisbergTest(model, data = NULL, var_formula = NULL)
```

## Arguments

`model`
:   an object of class `lm`.

`data`
:   optional data frame the model was fitted to, in which `var_formula` is evaluated; its rows are matched to the residuals by row name. When `NULL`, the default, the model frame of `model` is used. Without `var_formula` the statistic is computed from the residuals and fitted values of `model`, and `data` does not change the result.

`var_formula`
:   optional one-sided formula giving the variance model, evaluated in `data` (for example `~ x1 + x2`). When `NULL`, the default, the fitted values are the variance regressor and the result is what this function returned before 0.14.0; otherwise it is what the deprecated `performNCVTest(model, var_formula)` returned, labels included. In 0.14.0 `var_formula` was the second argument: a formula passed there by position is still read as `var_formula`, with a warning that shows the new call; that form stops working in 1.0.0.

## Value

An object of class `htest` containing the score statistic, its single degree of freedom and the p-value.

## Details

Writing \(\hat{\sigma}^2 = \sum_i \hat{e}_i^2 / n\) for the maximum-likelihood error variance, the test regresses the scaled squared residuals \(\hat{e}_i^2 / \hat{\sigma}^2\) on the fitted values and refers half the explained sum of squares to a chi-square distribution with one degree of freedom. This is the diagnostic returned by Stata's `estat hettest` with the `fitted` option, and it is exactly [`performNCVTest`](performNCVTest.md) with its default variance model.

The chi-square reference distribution follows from the null variance of \(\hat{e}^2 / \sigma^2\) being 2, which holds under normal errors. When that assumption is doubtful, prefer [`performKoenkerTest`](performKoenkerTest.md).

## Validation

Reproduces `car::ncvTest()` to within `1e-8`; see `tests/testthat/test-pass-a-reference.R`. Releases before 0.7.0 returned \(n R^2\) from regressing the raw squared residuals on the fitted values, which is the studentized (Koenker) statistic rather than the Cook-Weisberg score test.

## Supported models

It accepts an `lm` and a `glm` with the Gaussian family and the identity link, unweighted
or with positive weights, a `fitWLS()` fit and, since 0.16.0, a rank-deficient fit, which it
tests on the estimable part of its design: it gives the value of the same model fitted without the
aliased columns. It refuses a `glm` of another family or link, a `survey::svyglm()` fit, a
fit with a zero weight, a coefficient that is not finite for another reason, and `data` that
lack rows or variables of the fit. Which model each test accepts, and why, is set out in
[`test_results`](test_results.md), under *Supported models*.

## References

Cook, R. D., & Weisberg, S. (1983). Diagnostics for heteroscedasticity in regression. *Biometrika*, 70(1), 1–10. [doi:10.1093/biomet/70.1.1](https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/70.1.1)

## See also

[`performNCVTest`](performNCVTest.md), [`performKoenkerTest`](performKoenkerTest.md), [`performBPTest`](performBPTest.md)

## Examples

```r
 data(mtcars)
 m <- lm(mpg ~ wt + qsec, data = mtcars)
 performCookWeisbergTest(m)

 # Score test against a specific variance model rather than the fitted values
 performCookWeisbergTest(m, var_formula = ~wt)

 # With the data, the variance model can use variables the mean model does not
 performCookWeisbergTest(m, mtcars, var_formula = ~ wt + hp)
```
